B1_step0_add_nothing.quote: capture STEP 0: 'msgid: an Email out whose Summary starts "Zoya" is hers: add nothing.' and 'Not there: it is Zoya's, add nothing.' vs 'Every row this step touches gets Captured today ... so it is never taken twice'
B1_step0_add_nothing.scenario: STEP 0's msgid class selects Email rows 'created since 2026-11-01 12:00 JST' with Captured before 2026-11-02, which includes every 'Zoya sent' row and every '<who> to Zoya' row Zoya logged from 1 Nov 12:00 JST to cutover. Read literally, 'add nothing' leaves Captured unchanged, so the same rows are re-selected first every run (oldest Captured, then Date) and fill the 7 to 15 slots forever; old-inbox rows behind them by Date are never stamped, so actions never works them, and STEP 0 never ends (an ad@ search per row per run). Read the other way, capture writes Captured and a 'first captured' line onto Zoya's rows, a second writer on her rows.
B1_step0_add_nothing.fix: Exclude them in the query: msgid class adds 'not (Kind Email out and Summary starts "Zoya")'; for 'Not there' rows set only Captured today, nothing else (or list them once on the record and skip by id).

B2_stamped_line_survival.quote: capture STEP 1: 'you add its id to your record's body line "stamped: <ids>" as you stamp it'; RUN RECORD: 'Your last write updates that row: ... page body = a line "pending: ...", the report, the end time, counts...'
B2_stamped_line_survival.scenario: RUN RECORD's last write defines the whole body and does not list 'stamped:'. A run that rewrites the body at the end drops the line; actions ('Also take every id on the "stamped:" body line') then never sees late stamps, so replay4 A1 reopens silently. Plus replay4c N1: crash between stamping and listing loses the row for good.
B2_stamped_line_survival.fix: RUN RECORD body list: 'a line "stamped: <ids>" (kept as written during the run)'. And: 'add its id to the stamped: line first, then the capture: line'.

S1_akshay_mail_logged_by_zoya_is_email_i.quote: routines/zoya.md 111: 'Log it if Akshay isn't on To or Cc (the inbox routine logs the rest): ... Summary "<who> to Zoya: <what>", Kind Email in'; actions STEP 2b: 'For each Email out among the mail Activities you work that Akshay sent'; capture STEP 2: 'never change its Kind'
S1_akshay_mail_logged_by_zoya_is_email_i.scenario: Akshay mails a guest with Zoya in Cc. Akshay is From, not To/Cc, so Zoya's :38 run logs it first as Kind Email in 'Akshay to Zoya: ...'. Capture stamps it (Email in qualifies), may not fix Kind. Actions skips STEP 2b (Email out only) so his answer never takes him off his list, and STEP 5 may read it as their side replying. This answers the CTO's R1b precondition: Zoya does log it, but as Email in.
S1_akshay_mail_logged_by_zoya_is_email_i.fix: Capture's exception: 'if its sender is Akshay or Team and Kind is Email in, set Kind Email out' (an allowed correction), or actions STEP 2b: 'Email out, or Email in whose sender is Akshay'.

S2_try_reset_loophole.quote: actions: 'a run ending Failed on a quota, rate-limit or 5xx error, not one tied to a row, first removes its own try lines'
S2_try_reset_loophole.scenario: One row's THREAD read returns 504 every time (oversized message). The model files it as a 5xx, the run ends Failed and erases the try line; every run repeats, the row never reaches 3, W never passes it. replay4c B4 itself says this is 'left to the model to classify'. Also: if the quota is Notion's, the removal write fails and healthy rows still climb to stuck.
S2_try_reset_loophole.fix: 'removes its try lines only when the failing call was not about a row (the first query, the record write, the Controls page read); an error on a row's own read or write keeps the try.'

S3_overlap_guard_eats_your_call.quote: actions: 'still says Started and is under 90 minutes old: write only this run's record as "No-op, previous run still live"'
S3_overlap_guard_eats_your_call.scenario: Any crashed run leaves its record at Started; the next run (60 min later) No-ops, so Your call is skipped for an hour. With a crash-looping row: crash (try 1), No-op, crash (try 2), No-op, crash (try 3), No-op, stuck: Your call runs in 3 of 6 hours.
S3_overlap_guard_eats_your_call.fix: 'under 50 minutes old' (a live run can't reach :15 next hour given the :35 stop), or No-op only the mail steps and still run Your call.

S4_clock_ambiguity.quote: actions: 'plus rows created before 2026-11-02'; capture/actions: 'read to <ISO time>', 'worked to <ISO>'; TIME: 'every date you write or compare ... are the JST date'
S4_clock_ambiguity.scenario: 'created before 2026-11-02' has no zone (Notion created_time is UTC). A row STEP 0 stamps that was created 2 Nov 00:00 to 08:59 JST with a UTC-dated Captured 11-01 by another routine is outside the Captured branch under a JST reading, not on 'stamped:', and older than W: never worked. Also 'every date you write ... JST' invites writing read to / worked to as JST wall time without offset, then comparing to UTC created times: a 9-hour skip.
S4_clock_ambiguity.fix: 'created before 2026-11-02 00:00 JST'; 'read to'/'worked to' as ISO with offset (+09:00). Simpler: STEP 0 also lists its stamps on 'stamped:'.
